label: rem:chern-simons-as-knot-invariant
title: Classical Chern--Simons as a non-hyperbolic knot invariant
html:
Remark (Chern--Simons as a knot invariant).

Classical Chern--Simons theory does not serve as the bulk categorical action (comparison). That role belongs to \mathfrak{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q). Its archimedean image recovers Einstein--Hilbert, Yang--Mills, and Dirac. The Chern--Simons functional enters strictly as a geometric knot invariant. The commensurability class of the knot complement selects it.

The mechanism proceeds as follows:

  1. The trace of the coupling endomorphism P_{\mathrm{anti}} on a force-carrier knot configuration defines a Gram pairing at the J^2 jet layer.

  2. For hyperbolic knots, the Gram entry is the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) of the knot complement.

  3. For non-hyperbolic torus knots T_{m,n}, including the strong (T_{2,9}) and weak (T_{3,5}) force carriers, the hyperbolic volume vanishes. The classical Chern--Simons functional replaces it:

      \mathrm{CS}(T_{m,n})
  =
  \frac{\pi^2\, (m^2 - 1)(n^2 - 1)}{12\, m\, n}.

  4. The determinant ratio \kappa = \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{cl}} / \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{q} appears in the fine-structure correction 1/\alpha = q \cdot [9]_q [10]_q (1 + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}} + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2 \kappa). It exactly measures the classical-vs-q-deformed ratio of Chern--Simons pairings [witten2011].

Classical Chern--Simons is a derived geometric invariant, invoked only when the knot complement fails to be hyperbolic. Analytic continuation of Chern--Simons theory supplies its q-deformed counterpart G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{q} [witten2011].
